hypothesis: Iter 92 = two TEACHER defects found by measuring the simulator against LITERATURE (N=30-40 randomized patients, 65 g mixed meal), not against benchmark.dataset.generated.json -- which is a synthetic linear sweep of ONE archetype (user-02 = user-01 + 2.5 mg/dL at every point; glucose peaks exactly AT meal.time) and therefore cannot adjudicate physiology. (1) GHRELIN OVER-SUPPRESSION: postprandial nadir was -78% vs fasting; Cummings 2001 gives -30 to -50%. Two compounding causes. Production multiplied (1-insulin_supp) by (1-Ra_norm), which are two readings of the SAME postprandial event -- at the trough 0.354*0.166 = 0.059, so production collapsed to ~6% of basal. They are now a saturating union, so neither stacks past saturation, with insulin retained as a contributor so the registered insulin->ghrelin -1 coupling prior stays supported by the trajectory signal. And even ONE suppressor alone was too strong (Ra_norm implies ~-85% at equilibrium), so new ghr_supp_max=0.60 caps the suppressible fraction. Measured nadir -79.8% -> -41.0%. (2) POSTPRANDIAL TIMING LAG: three independent markers were late in the same direction, which is why this is ONE absorption-kernel defect and not three -- glucose peak 67.6 min (lit 45-60), insulin peak 73.3 (lit 30-60), ghrelin nadir 128 (lit 60-90). The gamma-2 carb kernel peaks at 1/rate, so meal_absorption_fast_rate=0.03 put appearance at 33 min; raised to 0.040. Sharpening also inflates peak AMPLITUDE (peak flux scales with rate, the kernel integral does not) and the amplitude was already correct at +47 mg/dL, so the shared *3.0 was split out as CARB_APPEARANCE_GAIN=2.55 on the CARB path only (fat/protein keep 3.0) to hold it. Measured: glucose peak -> 57.1 min with rise held at 46.9, insulin peak -> 62.7, ghrelin nadir -> 112, 4 h glucose residual 8.0 -> 5.1. NOT CHANGED, deliberately: k_ghr. Raising 0.02 -> 0.035 WOULD pull the ghrelin nadir into the 60-90 window, but k_ghr=0.02 implies half-life ln2/k = 35 min, matching ghrelin's measured plasma half-life (~30 min) -- that would contradict a directly measured constant to fix a downstream timing symptom. Same discipline that rejected the arterial baroreflex (d13b385) and the resting-HRV anchor. ALSO CLEARED this pass, so they are NOT targets: teacher insulin response magnitude (peak 52.6 uU/mL, lit 40-60) and resting glucagon (68.4 pg/mL, lit ~70) -- both previously suspected, both fine. And the cardiovascular axis was separately validated as literature-consistent with no remaining defect; the old 'post-exercise HRR too fast' claim was an n=1 false alarm (properly measured HRR1 = 22.0 bpm at maximal intensity, matching Cole 1999's healthy 20-30).
expectedEffect: PRIMARY: the trained student should reproduce the corrected teacher kinetics -- probe it with a single isolated 65 g mixed meal at the prior-mean embedding and check glucose peak lands 45-60 min (was ~58 in iter-91, teacher was 68) and ghrelin nadir lands -30 to -50% (teacher was -78%). GATE: this is a MODEL-QUALITY iteration, not a gate fix -- the gate already passes at PULSE_BENCHMARK_PRIOR_WEIGHT=0 (iter-91: glucose 0.151 hr 0.125 sbp 0.037 dbp 0.042 temp 0.019, overall_weighted_mape 0.077). PROTECT THAT. Sharper/earlier carb appearance and ~10% lower 3 h iAUC change the glucose trajectory shape, so glucose_mape is the marker most at risk; watch it and hr (which follows glucose through the metabolic->CVS coupling). A gate regression here would be the real cost of the change and should be weighed against the physiological gain. NOTE the benchmark cannot see a teacher change until retrain (benchmark.py never imports the teacher; the dataset is static with baked-in initial_state), which is exactly why this iteration had to be validated against literature + the cohort/textbook tests instead.
